steps.what: Locate and read the current exercise program or physiological testing procedure in the clinical exercise record system (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual participant identity and prescribed program or ordered test
existing approved procedure and precautions

steps.what: Explain exercise program or physiological testing procedures to participants, demonstrate as needed and check their understanding and questions
inputs: physiologist-read procedure and participant-specific precautions
participant's actual questions, language and demonstrated understanding
outputs: participant explanation, demonstration and checked understanding

tasks.design: Configure current procedure links in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the clinical exercise record system. The physiologist reads the actual procedure and adapts the live explanation and understanding check to the participant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the correct current instruction can interrupt the explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical record links can surface the current approved instruction.
tasks.still_hard: Comprehension, anxiety and participant-specific precautions require live judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise misunderstanding and respond to the participant.

ambition.what: No expansion of clinical scope assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0.5-1; clinical owner validates instructions and access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical record links can reduce navigation while a clinician retains explanation and comprehension checks.

assumptions: Unmeasured illustrative shares, not an observed baseline. Gross 15 x 0.10 = 1.5 hours per 100; incremental upkeep 0.5; net 1.0.
The approved instruction already exists, with a clinical owner maintaining it; no new instructions are generated or uncounted translation assumed.

This episode is the explanation itself. No separate report, send or record write is required by the statement or assumed locally; where a session note records this explanation it belongs to session documentation, not a second credited task.
Missing or ambiguous instructions require manual retrieval and clinical clarification. No saving from existing clinical software execution.
unknowns: Actual navigation burden and whether local documentation is required
research_questions: Does an observed explanation episode contain avoidable navigation, and is its documentation already included in session notes?

incremental.description: Maintain and spot-check native procedure links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 unmeasured navigation-only scenario; below 1.0% modeled net and zero if links already suffice.

steps.what: Read actual participant medical history, goals, assessment results and applicable standards and credentialing requirements in the clinical exercise record system (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual clinical history, participant goals and exercise assessments entered by their clinical producers
current exercise science standards, regulatory and credentialing requirements

steps.what: Develop exercise program choices, dose and progression to improve strength, flexibility, endurance or circulatory functioning within actual clinical and professional constraints
inputs: physiologist-reviewed source evidence and constraints
participant's actual preferences and tolerances
outputs: physiologist-selected exercises, dose, progression and monitoring criteria

steps.what: Enter and check the final exercise program, identity, clinical fit, standards compliance and destination record
inputs: physiologist-selected exercises, dose, progression and monitoring criteria
actual participant identifier and current record
outputs: exact final checked exercise program and destination record

steps.what: Save the exact checked exercise program in the intended participant record
inputs: exact final checked exercise program and destination record

tasks.design: Configure a participant source view and reuse fixed identity/reference fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the clinical exercise record system. The physiologist chooses the complete exercise prescription, enters and checks the final program, then saves that exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Navigation and re-entry of fixed identifiers can distract from program design.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and fixed-field reuse can reduce clerical effort.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical exercise choices and compliance require qualified judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Balance the participant's goals, physiological findings and risk.

ambition.what: No autonomous prescription or wider clinical scope.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; clinical governance approves access and field reuse

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: clinical record configuration can reuse fixed fields while clinical program decisions remain with the physiologist.

assumptions: Unmeasured illustrative shares. Gross 25 x .05 + 24 x .05 = 2.45; incremental upkeep .75; net 1.70 hours per 100.
Source records already exist from actual clinical producers; absent history or assessments must be obtained and reviewed manually, with no claimed benefit.
Only fixed identity/reference reuse is configured. Exercises, dose, progression and clinical conclusions are authored and checked by the physiologist.
Same-system save is approximately zero effort today, represented by 1 fully retained point with no saving. Program delivery or a later revision is a separate episode and no free send is promised.
Authoring check s3 gates only the exact final version and intended record; edits invalidate it. No separate self-approval ceremony.
unknowns: Existing record reuse and navigation time
research_questions: Which fields are actually retyped during program authoring rather than already filled?

steps.what: Review actual participant risk, current program and relevant session measurements in the clinical exercise record and monitoring system (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual current program, clinical precautions and available measurements from existing clinical devices and records

steps.what: Provide clinical oversight of exercise for participants at all risk levels, observing responses and intervening or seeking clinical support as needed
inputs: physiologist-reviewed participant context
actual participant condition, symptoms and exercise responses
outputs: observed exercise session and physiologist's actual clinical actions and findings

steps.what: Enter and check actual clinical exercise session findings, interventions and participant identity in the session record
inputs: observed exercise session and physiologist's actual clinical actions and findings
actual participant and session identifiers
outputs: exact checked session note and intended participant record

steps.what: Authenticate the exact checked session note in the intended clinical record
inputs: exact checked session note and intended participant record

tasks.design: Configure current-session views and fixed participant/session identifiers in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the clinical exercise record and monitoring system. Clinical oversight remains live; the physiologist writes the actual findings, checks the completed note and authenticates that version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Switching between clinical context and session entry adds navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native session views and identifier reuse can reduce that navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising deterioration and intervening across risk levels cannot be delegated to this configuration.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret participant response and act within clinical competence.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; clinical owner approves views and record access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native clinical session views can reduce navigation without replacing live supervision or note verification.

assumptions: Unmeasured documented-session scenario. Gross 15 x .05 + 19 x .05 = 1.70; upkeep .5; net 1.20 per 100 hours.
Actual session findings are produced by the physiologist in s2 and entered in s3; no new sensor feed, inferred findings or automatic narrative is assumed.
Existing device monitoring and alarms are already part of today's work and earn no saving. New escalation messages are not automated or credited.
Session documentation is split from live work, with all substantive writing retained. The same-system authentication click has 1 fully retained point and no saving.
Only s3's final note and identity check gates s4; edits require recheck. Do not add the explanation/history record again when it is the same session note.
unknowns: Actual session documentation burden and existing identifiers
research_questions: Are participant and session fields currently re-entered during documented oversight?

tasks.short: Interview participants and record history and goals

steps.what: Interview participants to obtain medical history or assess participant goals, probing and clarifying actual answers
inputs: actual participant account and questions
physiologist's history and goals questions
outputs: actual elicited history and participant goals with uncertainties

steps.what: Record and check actual participant medical history and goals in the clinical exercise record system (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual elicited history and participant goals with uncertainties
actual participant identity and existing record identifiers
outputs: exact final checked history/goals record and participant identity

steps.what: Save the exact checked history and goals in the intended participant record
inputs: exact final checked history/goals record and participant identity
outputs: saved participant medical history and goals

tasks.design: Configure fixed participant identifiers and a history/goals entry view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the clinical exercise record system. The physiologist elicits and records the actual account, resolves uncertainties and saves only the completed checked version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated identity entry adds clerical effort to recording the interview.
tasks.enabler_now: Native participant-context entry can reuse fixed identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive history, incomplete recall and goal assessment require conversation and judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Ask useful follow-up questions and distinguish reported from confirmed information.

ambition.what: No autonomous interview or clinical conclusion.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0.5-1; clinical owner approves access and entry fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native participant-context forms can reduce fixed-field entry while history elicitation and clinical checking remain human.

assumptions: Unmeasured documented-interview scenario. Gross 24 x .05 = 1.20; incremental upkeep .5; net .70 per 100 hours.
Participant produces the account in s1 and physiologist captures and checks it in s2. No ambient recording, pre-existing structured answers or generated missing history is assumed.
Clinical prose and uncertainty checking remain fully human; only fixed identity entry/navigation changes. If native context already exists there is no saving.
Same-system save takes approximately zero time today, represented as 1 fully retained point without saving. Final authoring check s2 gates that exact record; edits invalidate it.
Count this record once if the same history/goals content is already in the session note under oversight.
unknowns: Actual duplicate identifier entry and overlap with session documentation
research_questions: Which interview record fields are genuinely re-entered, and where is the single authoritative note?

approvals.approved_version: Exact final history/goals content and participant record checked in s2; any edit requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 provisional identity-entry reduction below .70% modeled net; no live interview saving.
